history.dynasty: Nath monastic lineage (present structure shaped under Mahants Digvijaynath and Avedyanath in the 19th century)
history.period: c. 11th-12th century origins (traditional); present structure 19th century
history.summary: Gorakhnath Math is the principal seat of the Nath tradition, dedicated to Yogi Gorakhnath (c. 11th century), disciple of Matsyendranath and a founder of Hatha Yoga. The city of Gorakhpur takes its name from him. The temple complex holds his samadhi shrine and gaddi; the math runs a second temple in Gorkha district, Nepal. Temple records say the structure was destroyed twice (by Alauddin Khilji in the 14th century and Aurangzeb in the 18th century) and rebuilt; the current form dates to 19th-century work under the mahants. Note: the destruction accounts come from temple tradition, not independently verified historical records.

name: Gorakhnath Temple
town_description: Gorakhpur is a major city in eastern Uttar Pradesh (Purvanchal), on the Rapti river, named after Yogi Gorakhnath. It is a cultural and religious hub with Gorakhnath Math as its best-known shrine, and a rail and road gateway to Nepal and the Terai.
